name: Pallas Textiles
old_description: Inspired by Claude Monet and the gardens of Giverny, our newest collection translates fleeting light, softened color, and painterly
about:
Pallas Textiles operates from Green Bay, Wisconsin. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, and no founders are named in public materials.

The company produces upholsteries, panel fabrics, and privacy curtains by fusing traditional weaving with modern fiber techniques. Collections such as Giverny — inspired by Claude Monet’s gardens — translate painterly gestures into textured textiles. Pallas manages a sample program offering color and pattern swatches, and maintains a network of sales representatives across the United States and internationally.

Its textiles serve healthcare environments, commercial interiors, and contract furniture manufacturers; the company notes KI products approved for its Monet pattern. Pallas exhibits at events such as the Healthcare Design Expo and hosts design workshops where clients create bags, pillows, and other items using its fabrics.

Pallas describes its approach as “Made True,” emphasizing genuine materials and authentic people. It positions its point of difference as the marriage of artisanal weaving heritage with contemporary fiber technology to deliver curated colors, nature‑inspired patterns, and performance suited to healing spaces.
